newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds follow core European markets lower.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds follow core European markets lower.

text.p: Irish bonds were marked down slightly in thin afternoon trade in line with a weaker performance by core European markets following remarks from French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, dealers said.

"We started out this morning in good shape and saw some convergence but since then we've seen some Irish selling and some falling off in core Europe," a dealer said. "Jospin seems to have muddied the waters over EMU."
By 1510 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 12 pence at 101.93 to yield 5.97 percent, while the eight percent bond due 2006 was down 20 pence at 109.60 to yield 6.57 percent.
Yields against German Bunds were broadly unchanged from the close at 156 basis points over in the five-year bond, and 82 over in the 10-year.
A barrage of remarks from France's Jospin earlier had led to choppy action on currency, equity, and bond markets in Europe, traders said.

Jospin said further cuts in service sector jobs would be halted, and proposed a four percent increase in the minimum wage and a decrease in the working week to 35 hours, while also reiterating his commitment to an on-time kickoff to European economic and monetary union.
Dealers said Jospin's remarks created uncertainty for France's economic outlook.

"The negative side of Jospin's speech is that it looks like he's not taking the (EMU) deficit criterion too seriously," one dealer said. "In fact he's outlining expenditure plans -- where's the money going to come from? We can't have EMU without France."
Dealers largely shrugged off a surge in the Philadelphia Federal Reserve's June business activity index released earlier, which jumped to 25.2 from 1.6 in May.
